## Strings
::::::: columns
::::: {.column width="50%"}
:::: {style="font-size: 65%;"}
::: incremental
- Series of key strokes:
  - abcd1234
  - Hello World
- Good to avoid spaces (command: argument + parameter)
  - Hello_World
- Data type - integer, boolean, list, array
- Store in a variable
- Access with `$` prefix
  - Print value of variable with `echo`
:::
::::
:::::

::: {.fragment .column width="\"50%"}

::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
foo="Hello World"
echo foo
echo $foo

bar=Goodbye Sky
echo $bar
```


::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
foo
Hello World
bash: line 4: Sky: command not found
```


:::
:::

::::{style="font-size: 65%;"}
::::: incremental
- Why does `bar=Goodbye Sky` break?
:::::
::::
:::
:::::::

## Paths
::::::: columns
::::: {.column width="50%"}
:::: {style="font-size: 65%;"}
::: incremental
- File paths can be stored in variable
- Two types:
  - Relative - start current location
  - Absolute - start at root
- Special path: PATH
  - Search path of executables
  - Reveal command path with `which`
:::
::::
:::::

::::: {.column width="\"50%"}
::: {layout-nrow="2"}
![](abs_rel_path.png){.fragment} ![](bash_path.png){.fragment}
:::
:::::
::::::::


## Brace expansion
::::::: columns
::::: {.column width="50%"}
:::: {style="font-size: 65%;"}
::: incremental
- Curly braces containing a list: '`{1..4}`'
- Expand sequential or comma-separated lists
- Append to strings - easy file, directory generation
  - E.g. '`mkdir -p sub-{1..3}`'
- Combine to generate permutations
  - E.g. '`for i in pref-{1..3}{a..c}; do ...`'
- Supports nesting
- Run in subshell '`$()`' to store in variable

:::
::::
:::::

::::: {.fragment .column width="\"50%"}

::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
echo {a..d}
echo sub-{1..3}
perm=$(echo {1..3}{a..c})
nest=$(echo pref-{foo,bar{1..3},baz})
echo $perm
echo $nest
```


::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
a b c d
sub-1 sub-2 sub-3
1a 1b 1c 2a 2b 2c 3a 3b 3c
pref-foo pref-bar1 pref-bar2 pref-bar3 pref-baz
```


:::
:::

:::::
::::::::

## Combining variables
::::::: columns
::::: {.column width="50%"}
:::: {style="font-size: 65%;"}
::: incremental
- Access variables with '`$`'
- Combine with curly braces to:
  - Add suff/prefix:
    - '`var=foo; echo ${var}bar`'
  - Combine variables
    - '`var1=foo; var2=bar; echo ${var1}$var2`'
  - Note: reuse of '{}' - key-bindings are context dependent!
:::
::::
:::::

::::: {.fragment .column width="\"50%"}

::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
var1=foo; var2=bar
echo "1 ${var1}baz"
echo "2 ${var1}$var2"
echo "3 $var1$var2"
echo "4 $var1baz"
```


::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
1 foobaz
2 foobar
3 foobar
4 
```


:::
:::


::::{style="font-size: 65%;"}
::: incremental
- Why does '`echo "4 $var1baz"`' break?
:::
::::
:::::
::::::::

## Slice: front
::::::: columns
::::: {.column width="50%"}
:::: {style="font-size: 65%;"}
::: incremental
- Often desirable to slice strings
  - E.g. extract "awesome" from "I_am_awesome"
- Extracting subject, session, or task from file name
  - BIDS: sub-1_ses-A_task-memory
- Combine "#" and string with variable call to slice from string beginning
  - "#" removes before first string match
  - Wildcard symbol "*" matches anything
  - "##" removes before final string match
:::
::::
:::::

::::: {.fragment .column width="\"50%"}

::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
bids_name=sub-1_ses-A_task-memory
echo $bids_name
echo ${bids_name#*_}
echo ${bids_name##*_}

```


::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
sub-1_ses-A_task-memory
ses-A_task-memory
task-memory
```


:::
:::


::::{style="font-size: 65%;"}
::: incremental
- What would '`echo ${bids_name#*-}`' say?
- How about '`echo ${bids_name#sub-1}`'?
- How about '`echo ${bids_name##*-}`'?
:::
::::
:::::
::::::::

## Slice: back

::::::: columns
::::: {.column width="50%"}
:::: {style="font-size: 65%;"}
::: incremental
- The "%" is used to slice from the back
  - "%" removes after last string match
  - "%%" removes after first string match
- An intermediate variable can be used to extract string middle
:::
::::
:::::

::::: {.fragment .column width="\"50%"}

::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
bids_name=sub-1_ses-A_task-memory
echo $bids_name
echo ${bids_name%_*}
echo ${bids_name%%_*}
int=${bids_name#*_}
echo ${int%_*}
```


::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
sub-1_ses-A_task-memory
sub-1_ses-A
sub-1
ses-A
```


:::
:::

:::::
::::::::

## Slice: positional

::::::: columns
::::: {.column width="50%"}
:::: {style="font-size: 65%;"}
::: incremental
- Each character in a string has a position
  - 0-indexed, abcd = 0123
- Use ":" to specify start and end of positions
:::
::::
:::::

::::: {.fragment .column width="\"50%"}

::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
alpha="abcdefg"
echo ${alpha:0:3}
echo ${alpha:3}
```


::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
abc
defg
```


:::
:::


::::{style="font-size: 65%;"}
::: incremental
- What would '`echo ${alpha:1:4}`' say?
- What would '`echo ${alpha:5}`' say?
:::
::::
:::::
::::::::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
